title: Ongoing
description: Which local projects deserve attention: one API, two clients, a cache-first scanner, and an app-owned catalog.
provenance: Authored 2026-09-11 from the Ongoing source tree, ADRs, README, AGENTS.md, deployment and website docs. Every component cites the files inspected. The catalog repository is modeled as one component rather than per table; the Svelte component tree and the test suites are intentionally shallow. The tech radar subsystem is a proposal from docs/plans/tech-radar.md and is not built.

boundaries.title: Same HTTP contract
boundaries.description: Both clients go through the JSON API. A capability reachable only through the browser would be a design bug.

boundaries.title: LAN request boundary
boundaries.description: Every request crosses the production edge and the SvelteKit gate: bounded bodies, security headers, and, when enabled, session and same-origin checks. Auth is intentionally off in production.

boundaries.title: Pure rules, no I/O
boundaries.description: Functions of normalized data only. The browser re-runs attention classification after an optimistic edit without repository access.

boundaries.title: One scan at a time
boundaries.description: Two processes open the same SQLite file. The durable scan lease in scan_runs, heartbeated every 10 seconds, keeps a manual scan from overlapping the calendar job.

boundaries.title: Subprocess and network egress
boundaries.description: Everything that spawns a tool or leaves the machine. Each path has a timeout and an availability state; none can fail a whole scan.

boundaries.title: App-owned durable state
boundaries.description: Ongoing's SQLite file and the release tooling that backs it up, migrates it, and restores it. Never a repository's .todos database.

boundaries.title: Public website copy
boundaries.description: The only data that leaves the private dashboard: explicitly included website records, exported deterministically, without notes, paths, or scanned metrics.

scenes.title: Ongoing at a glance
scenes.description: One local process serves a browser and a CLI from an app-owned catalog that a bounded scanner keeps fresh.

scenes.title: One API, two clients
scenes.description: The CLI and the browser are peers: both read page models and send mutations through the same routes, behind the same gate.

scenes.title: How a scan refreshes the catalog
scenes.description: Discovery first, then git, TD, and stack per project, cloc only when the worktree changed, then release baselines and GitHub once per run.

scenes.title: From cached rows to attention views
scenes.description: The read model joins catalog tables, resolves stacks against baselines, and asks the pure domain rules which views each project belongs to and why.

scenes.title: Tools, APIs, and hosts
scenes.description: What Ongoing spawns, calls, or is scheduled by, and how each dependency is allowed to fail.

scenes.title: Running on aerie.local
scenes.description: Two launchd agents, one pinned Bun, a health-gated deploy that quiesces both before touching the database.

scenes.title: Boundaries and authority
scenes.description: Where requests are gated, which code is pure, who may hold the scan lease, what leaves the machine, and what is allowed to go public.

scenes.title: Proposal: technologies as catalog entries
scenes.description: A sketched second entry kind with rings and project edges, detected by the stack collector and exposed through ongoing tech.
